the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The ringed space (E, O_X|_E) is locally ringed, so the morphism-into-affine lemma applies to the identity A = Gamma(E, O_X|_E) and produces the canonical morphism j into Spec(A). Write E as the intersection of a nonempty directed family of quasi-compact opens U_i of X and set A_i = Gamma(U_i, O_{U_i}). For each i there is a commutative square from (E, O_X|_E) and (U_i, O_{U_i}) into Spec(A) and Spec(A_i). Since U_i is quasi-affine, U_i to Spec(A_i) is a quasi-compact open immersion; since A = colim A_i, Spec(A) = lim Spec(A_i) as topological spaces (limits-lemma-topology-limit); and E = lim U_i (topology-lemma-make-spectral-space). Hence E to Spec(A) is a homeomorphism onto its image E', and E' is the intersection of the inverse images of the opens U_i of Spec(A_i); moreover for every e in E the local ring O_{X, e} equals the value of O_{U_i, e}, which agrees with the value on Spec(A). For the final assertion pick i, j with U_i inside U_j and consider the three commutative squares for U_i and W over Spec(A_i) and Spec(A_j) and over Spec(A). By properties-lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine the first square is cartesian, hence so is the second, and passing to the limit the third is cartesian, so the top horizontal arrow W to Spec(A) is an open immersion; that is, j(W) is open in Y.
